Will — thanks for the clear asks. High-level answers below; I'll attach a compact estimate and a suggested MAP update. We should treat these as conservative planning figures for procurement. If you want a tighter cost/op latency tradeoff we can run a short eval on your representative prompt set (2–3 days).

Summary (short):
- Dedicated (hosted Redwood Dedicated, reserved H100 pool): lead time for guaranteed committed tranche: 6–10 weeks from signed reservation (depends on region and current allocation windows).
- Private (customer-managed on-prem or VPC private deploy with customer hardware procurement): lead time driven by your procurement + hardware delivery and on-prem installation: typically 10–16 weeks for new H100 racks. Add 2–4 weeks for on-site validation with our private agent bundle.

Rightsizing (target 120 qps, 95p < 250ms): conservative starting recommendation:
- H100 equip-equivalent: 8–10 GPUs for steady-state to hit 120 qps under continuous small-batch traffic (batch size=8 typical).
- Add 30% buffer for peak bursts and model warmup windows → target pool: 11–13 GPUs.
- Canary / headroom for rolling upgrades → plan one extra GPU as a hot spare in the pool.

Notes: exact numbers vary with model (e.g., Llama2-70B vs smaller fine-tuned models), max sequence length, and KV-cache hit rates. I'll include a CSV with scenario rows (attached).

Next steps proposed in MAP:
- Week 0 (sign): Reservation committed (or PO for private hardware).
- Week 1–2: Kickoff, credentials & security questionnaire.
- Week 2–4: Eval window for latency/cost on your dataset (optional but recommended).
- Week 4–8: Provisioning & initial capacity (dedicated pools) or coordinate courier/hardware (private).
- Week 8–12+: Acceptance testing and canary roll to production.

I'll update the MAP doc and send a compact procurement-friendly summary for your finance/proc team.

-Neha

Will — quick answers and a proposed MAP amendment below. Priyom, feel free to jump in with pricing / legal caveats.

1) Staged provisioning: yes — Redwood Dedicated supports tranche-based activation. Typical pattern: initial 6-GPU tranche (provisioned within 3–4 weeks), followed by auto-provision of additional tranche(s) at negotiated calendar milestones. Staging reduces initial lead time and helps your finance cadence.

2) Worst-case activation window: if signed this month and region capacity is constrained, plan for up to 10 weeks for full committed pool activation for the full tranche. For staged 6-GPU initial activation can be as fast as 3–4 weeks. We'll commit to regular cadence updates during provisioning.

3) Procurement one-pager: attached (Orion_MAP_v3.docx) — includes acceptance criteria, checklist for SOC2 evidence, network allowlist steps, and a minimal lab/endpoint test script for performance verification.

MAP amendment (proposed language you can paste into your internal docs):
- Commitment: Customer signs reservation for X H100-equivalent GPUs.
- Staging: Initial tranche = 6 GPUs (activation target 3–4 weeks post-signature). Remaining tranche(s) activated per mutually agreed milestone (target full activation by week 10).
- Acceptance: 7 business day acceptance window after provisioning for performance & correctness tests.
- Canary: Redwood will support a rolling canary deployment with 10% traffic shift for 48 hours before full cutover.

If that works I'll push an updated MAP into the shared Drive and create a short quote.

-Ben
